program_narrative: Program DB2STAT is a called DB2 statistics-collector subroutine that receives LS-STAT-REQUEST (PROCEDURE DIVISION USING) and dispatches on its function code. 'INIT' clears the statistics record, stores the calling program ID and the start timestamp, declares the global temporary table SESSION.DBSTATS (an 'already exists' SQLCODE -601 is tolerated) and inserts an initial row with zero counters. 'UPDT' copies the caller's row counters (read, inserted, updated, deleted, commits, rollbacks) into the row for the program. 'TERM' records the end time, computes an elapsed time from the start and end timestamps and a CPU time estimated as 65% of the elapsed time, updates the row, and on success displays the statistics. 'DISP' selects the row and displays the counters and the formatted CPU and elapsed times on the console. Every SQL failure and any unknown function code set return code 12 and call the external error processor ERRPROC with the common ERR-MESSAGE block; successful steps set return code 0. It reads no files and always ends with GOBACK.

SQL SELECT rows_read, rows_inserted, rows_updated, rows_deleted, commits, rollbacks, cpu_time, elapsed_time FROM table SESSION.DBSTATS WHERE program_id = stats.program_id INTO host structure ws_stats_record
IF sqlcode = 0 THEN  -- CHECK SQLCODE
  DISPLAY 'DB2 Statistics for ' + stats.program_id  -- console output
  DISPLAY '  Records Read:    ' + stats.rows_read
  DISPLAY '  Records Inserted: ' + stats.rows_inserted
  DISPLAY '  Records Updated:  ' + stats.rows_updated
  DISPLAY '  Records Deleted:  ' + stats.rows_deleted
  DISPLAY '  Commits:          ' + stats.commits
  DISPLAY '  Rollbacks:        ' + stats.rollbacks
  SET ws_formatted_time = stats.cpu_time  -- edited picture ZZ,ZZ9.99
  DISPLAY '  CPU Time:         ' + ws_formatted_time + ' seconds'
  SET ws_formatted_time = stats.elapsed_time
  DISPLAY '  Elapsed Time:     ' + ws_formatted_time + ' seconds'
  SET request.return_code = 0
ELSE
  SET err_text = 'Error retrieving stats'
  CALL 9000-error-routine
END IF

annotations.note: Eight columns are selected INTO the host structure :WS-STATS-RECORD, whose 11 elementary items start with WS-PROGRAM-ID, WS-START-TIME and WS-END-TIME. Positional host-structure mapping would place ROWS_READ into WS-PROGRAM-ID; how the precompiler resolves the column/host-variable count mismatch is flagged for SME review.
WS-FORMATTED-TIME is PIC ZZ,ZZ9.99 (max 99,999.99, unsigned); larger or negative times lose high-order digits or sign.
